facts.value: An emergency is an urgent, unexpected, and usually dangerous situation that poses an immediate risk to health, life, property, or environment and requires immediate action.
facts.programme_association: Emergency Management and Homeland Security Degree | ASU Online

facts.value: An incident, to be an emergency, conforms to one or more conditions if it poses an immediate threat to life, health, property, or environment; has already caused loss of life, health detriments, property damage, or environmental damage; or has a high probability of escalating to cause immediate danger.
facts.programme_association: Emergency Management and Homeland Security Degree | ASU Online

facts.value: Most developed countries operate three core emergency services: Police, Fire, and Medical, to handle crime-related emergencies, fire-related emergencies, and medical-related emergencies respectively.
facts.programme_association: Emergency Management and Homeland Security Degree | ASU Online

facts.value: There may also be specialized emergency services, which can include bomb disposal, search and rescue, and hazardous material operations.
facts.programme_association: Emergency Management and Homeland Security Degree | ASU Online

facts.value: Most countries have an emergency telephone number, such as 911 in the United States, 999 in the United Kingdom, 112 in Europe, and 000 in Australia.
facts.programme_association: Emergency Management and Homeland Security Degree | ASU Online

facts.value: Domestic emergency services can consist of small, medium or large businesses who attend emergencies within the boundaries of licensing or capabilities for a fee.
facts.programme_association: Emergency Management and Homeland Security Degree | ASU Online

facts.value: Emergency action principles are key 'rules' that guide the actions of rescuers and potential rescuers in emergencies.
